text: The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes is a German scholarship organization founded in 1925, re-established in 1948 after being dissolved under National Socialism. It offers general scholarships for undergraduate and graduate studies, as well as doctoral scholarships, to students from around the world, with no citizenship or age restrictions. Applicants are selected through various channels, including school nominations, professor nominations, examination board nominations, and self-identification via an assessment test, based on academic excellence, initiative, and responsibility. The scholarship includes financial support (a monthly allowance, need-based subsidies, and partial tuition coverage) and academic support (summer schools, research groups, language courses, and mentoring). As of 2023, it awarded 2,179 undergraduate and 301 doctoral scholarships, with 71.5% of scholars receiving a study expense allowance. The organization also offers internal and open scholarship programs in collaboration with other institutions. Notable alumni include prominent scientists, scholars, and public figures in fields such as natural sciences, social sciences, business, and the arts. The Studienstiftung emphasizes academic and personal development, with a mission rooted in excellence and societal contribution.
